# Code of Conduct

ZeaZDev aims to keep technical collaboration professional, inclusive, evidence-based, and safe for contributors and users.

This organization-wide policy applies unless a repository defines a more specific code of conduct.

## Expected Behavior

We expect participants to:

- communicate respectfully and focus criticism on ideas, code, behavior, and evidence;
- assume good faith while still verifying technical claims;
- provide actionable review feedback;
- acknowledge uncertainty and correct mistakes when new evidence appears;
- respect privacy, confidentiality, licenses, and security boundaries;
- avoid harassment, intimidation, personal attacks, discriminatory language, or unwanted sexual attention;
- avoid publishing another person's private information without permission;
- avoid deliberately disrupting project infrastructure, discussions, or community spaces.

## Technical Disagreement

Strong technical disagreement is welcome when it remains constructive. Prefer reproducible examples, measurements, tests, standards, threat models, and documented constraints over personal judgments.

Maintainers may close or redirect discussions that are repeatedly off-topic, abusive, misleading, or disruptive.

## Security and Privacy

Do not use public discussions to expose credentials, private data, exploitable vulnerability details, or confidential information. Follow the project's security reporting process instead.

## Enforcement

Maintainers may edit, hide, remove, lock, or close content and may restrict participation when behavior materially violates this policy or threatens the safety or integrity of the project/community.

Serious or repeated violations may result in temporary or permanent removal from project spaces.

## Scope

This policy applies in repositories, issues, pull requests, reviews, discussions, and other spaces managed on behalf of ZeaZDev.
